name: Ellen Scott
life: “I still remember an old football shoe that touched only three toes.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Ellen by a small Friday habit. Ellen checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I ran barefoot races here. I want to know whether the old starting mark lies under that plank.
appearance: Ellen has a softly rounded chin under sharp cheekbones. Look for closely cropped salt-and-pepper hair. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a red windbreaker with a pen clipped inside the neckline. In conversation Ellen folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
personality: Ellen loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To locate the old racing start line.
family: Yvette Weber is Ellen’s cousin. Ellen makes the call. Yvette is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The last home visit*, Yvette says, “I want the new worker to knock twice. A single knock still sounds like a debt collector at my old front door.”
connections: Emery Holland. A saved tracing gives the runner somewhere to look for the buried starting mark.

reactions.situation: A child wants to trace a different sort of foot
reactions.response: Ellen gives the child paper and room for a footprint that goes home with them.
